================================================================================
EGZOS — DECISIONS LOG · v0.7 AMENDMENT SET
Delta on top of the v0.4 log and the v0.5 and v0.6 amendment sets. Records
the Chief's calls of 2026-10-22/23 and 2026-10-25: buy, don't build;
Supabase for the platform services; one login; the Face ID / Touch ID
confirm; places and git-like sync; the egzosux experience; Stripe; the
repository's visibility; where a hosted container's state lives and runs. Sections
not mentioned carry forward unchanged. Compiled 2026-10-23; §AF added
2026-10-25.
Read together with: egzos-decisions-log-v0.4.txt · egzos-decisions-v0.5-
amendments.txt · egzos-decisions-v0.6-amendments.txt · egzos-handoff.txt ·
egzos-build-plan-v1.2.txt
================================================================================

Status key:  [DECIDED] locked · [LEAN] stated preference, not locked ·
             [LATER] decided in direction, not scheduled ·
             [OPEN→CHIEF] explicitly awaiting the Chief's call


================================================================================
R. BUY, DON'T BUILD (new; binds every agent and the operator)
================================================================================

[DECIDED] IF A WIDELY USED SERVICE OR LIBRARY DOES THE JOB, WE USE IT. Login,
          OAuth, sessions, passkeys, databases, file storage, payments,
          hosting, DNS, email, queues, cloud-storage connectors and crypto
          primitives are bought (a paid service, or a maintained open-source
          project), never built. We build only what egzos IS: the node model
          and resolver, the trust rules and the gate, the ledger, the
          container contract, sync between places, and the experience.

[DECIDED] BUILDING A COMMODITY PIECE NEEDS THE CHIEF'S EXPLICIT YES, recorded
          in this log. An issue or PR that would build one says so in its
          first line and names the service it passed over and why. A review
          that finds commodity infrastructure built without that record
          raises it as a finding.

[DECIDED] Recorded as the reason for this rule: the container's own OAuth 2.1
          authorization server (§K, v0.6) was built slice by slice for
          weeks without the build-or-buy question being put to the Chief.
          It is retired in §S.


================================================================================
S. PLATFORM SERVICES — SUPABASE (supersedes v0.6 §K's own-AS decision;
   amends v0.5 §C and R3's "server-side stack chosen at Phase 6")
================================================================================

[DECIDED] SUPABASE IS THE ONE VENDOR for everything it covers:
          - login (Supabase Auth);
          - agent sign-in: Supabase's OAuth 2.1 server issues MCP clients
            their tokens (PKCE, dynamic client registration); egzos.io hosts
            the consent page it redirects to;
          - the hosted database (Postgres);
          - file storage (Supabase Storage: S3-compatible, signed URLs,
            files up to 500 GB on paid plans);
          - server-side glue such as payment webhooks (Edge Functions).
          Self-hosters run the open-source Supabase for the same parts.

[DECIDED] THE CONTAINER'S OWN AUTHORIZATION SERVER IS RETIRED. No further
          slices. authorization-server.md leaves the contract set; the
          unmounted code under src/egzos/authz/** is removed in the PR that
          lands Supabase token verification. Device-code for the CLI is
          retired with it: the CLI keeps its local token, and signs in to a
          cloud through Supabase.

[DECIDED] THE CONTAINER IS A RESOURCE SERVER. It verifies Supabase-issued
          JWTs (issuer, signature against the project's published keys,
          expiry) and maps them to a principal:
          - a user session (no client) → principal: interactive, with the
            role the container grants that user;
          - an OAuth-issued agent token → principal: client, with the role
            and scopes the container's agent registry grants that client.
          Supabase does not bind tokens to a resource (no RFC 8707), so the
          container also checks the client against its own registry; an
          unregistered client is refused like any unknown token (silence-
          not-errors holds).

[DECIDED] LOCALS STAY LOCAL. A local container keeps SQLite, the blob store
          on disk, its local token, MCP over stdio, and works offline. The
          Supabase parts serve clouds and the sign-in to them.

[DECIDED] STORAGE BACKENDS SIT BEHIND APACHE OpenDAL (one library for local
          disk, S3 and Supabase Storage today, and Azure Blob, GCS and the
          rest for §V's Cloud 2), not one adapter per provider.

[LEAN]    HOSTING for the hosted container: a managed host (Fly.io), with
          Cloudflare for DNS. Accounts and payment are the Chief's.


================================================================================
T. ONE LOGIN (supersedes R2 and v0.6 §K "two authorities")
================================================================================

[DECIDED] LOGGING IN TO egzos.io IS LOGGING IN TO YOUR CONTAINER. The
          container trusts the egzos Supabase project as its identity
          provider, and the browser presents the user's Supabase session to
          the container directly. Double login is retired.

[DECIDED] Accepted tradeoff, on record: the egzos Supabase project can now
          sign a session the user's container accepts, so egzos's identity
          provider is in the trust path of every container that uses it. A
          container owner can point the container at a different identity
          provider (a self-hoster's own Supabase); egzos's is the default.

[DECIDED] What stays: the browser talks to the container directly. egzos
          servers never proxy, cache or store a user's container data, and
          never call a user's container on their own authority. For a
          bring-your-own container the data plane still never touches egzos
          servers.


================================================================================
U. THE CONFIRM — FACE ID / TOUCH ID (amends R11's step-up and v0.6 §K's
   presence LEAN; closes v0.6 open question 6)
================================================================================

[DECIDED] A MOVE OR COPY THAT CHANGES WHO CAN SEE SOMETHING ASKS RIGHT THERE,
          inline: who will newly see it, then confirm. No separate page, no
          localhost tap window.

[DECIDED] THE CONFIRM IS THE DEVICE'S OWN BIOMETRIC: Face ID, Touch ID or
          Windows Hello, through WebAuthn with user verification required.
          Where the device has none, a plain confirm button. The audit event
          records which proof was given (biometric or button), so the ledger
          shows the weaker one for what it is. The button is a human act: it
          is refused to an agent's token (principal: client), so an agent
          driving a browser cannot confirm on the human's behalf.

[DECIDED] BUILT ON ESTABLISHED PIECES (§R): the browser's WebAuthn API and a
          maintained WebAuthn library to verify the assertion, or Supabase
          Auth's own WebAuthn support where it covers re-verification. No
          home-made challenge protocol.

[LATER]   PASSKEY SIGN-IN as an opt-in (Supabase Auth passkeys, in beta
          since May 2026).

[DECIDED] The step-up window (R11, ≈5 minutes per ring pair) carries over to
          the confirm unchanged.


================================================================================
V. PLACES AND SYNC (new; amends the storage contract at the next contract
   version)
================================================================================

[DECIDED] A CONTAINER HAS PLACES: one hosted cloud and any number of locals
          (a laptop, a desktop). Each project has a home place.

[DECIDED] SYNC IS GIT-LIKE, NOT LIVE: a local pushes what it has and pulls
          ("catches up") what it lacks, when asked; `status` says what is
          ahead and behind. Each place keeps its own ledger, and a push is
          verified on arrival (its hash chain) before it lands.

[DECIDED] COPY JOINS MOVE as a verb. Both run the gate: a copy that widens
          the audience is confirmed exactly like a move (§U).

[DECIDED] ORDER: one hosted cloud plus locals that push and pull come first.

[LATER]   CLOUD 2 — BRING YOUR OWN CLOUD: a user enters connection details
          for their own Azure, AWS or other storage, and it appears as a
          space they can upload into and import from, without an agent (the
          Chief's work Azure environment is the first case). Cloud
          containers become multi-backend. Built on OpenDAL (§S).

[LATER]   THE RELAY AND LIVE SYNC as an opt-in for users who want continuous
          sync. The idea is kept; it is not scheduled.


================================================================================
W. THE EXPERIENCE — egzosux (amends R3, R10 and §P of v0.6)
================================================================================

[DECIDED] THE egzosux PROTOTYPE (Egzos/egzosux) IS THE EXPERIENCE SPEC, SET
          BY THE CHIEF. Binding as experience, not as final visuals:
          - a 3D space; clouds and locals (locals as houses); the egzos orb,
            the ether that content sinks into; agents as pyramids;
          - navigation cloud → project → thread → artifacts;
          - move or copy an artifact to another thread, another project, or
            loose in a project;
          - XR.
          It supersedes the flagship's 2D screen specs as the flow; visual
          direction stays open and keeps flowing through the tokens.

[DECIDED] THE BUILT-IN CURATOR AGENT IS J4S (short for Jarvis), not "Chief".
          "Chief" names the human gate only.

[DECIDED] STACK (amends R3): TypeScript, three.js on its WebGL renderer
          (WebGPU is not used), React for the panels, Vite 8, WebXR. Tailwind
          and the tokens for the panels' chrome.

[DECIDED] ALL FRONT-END WORK LIVES IN Egzos/egzos-platform. egzosux stays the
          reference prototype; nothing is built on it in place. One component
          set, one tokens file, consistent and standardized across screens.

[DECIDED] THE egzos.io HOMEPAGE HOSTS THE EXPERIENCE AS A LIVE DEMO, on
          sample data, that a visitor can use before signing up. The
          homepage is decluttered and built on the same stack and the same
          3D code as the app, so the demo and the product cannot drift. The
          old demo site is replaced, not restyled.


================================================================================
X. BILLING — STRIPE BEHIND A PROVIDER INTERFACE (amends v0.5 §C)
================================================================================

[DECIDED] STRIPE handles payments: Stripe Checkout to subscribe, the Stripe
          customer portal to manage, webhooks into Supabase. egzos builds no
          payment form or invoice screen that Stripe already hosts.

[DECIDED] egzos code talks to a payments-provider interface, not to Stripe
          directly, so a second provider can be added later without
          rewriting billing.


================================================================================
Y. REPOSITORY VISIBILITY AND DISCLOSURE (amends v0.6 §L)
================================================================================

[DECIDED] Egzos/egzos IS PUBLIC AGAIN (the Chief, 2026-10-23), after a
          private interval in October 2026. §L's disclosure mechanics apply
          again: unfixed security findings are private GitHub Security
          Advisories; the regression test enters adversarial/ only in the
          fix PR. Egzos/egzos-platform stays private; its security findings
          stay issues there (its CLAUDE.md).


================================================================================
Z. RETENTION — NO AUTOMATIC DELETION (amends R11's staged-blob retention)
================================================================================

[DECIDED] Nothing is deleted automatically when a retention period ends.
          Staged bytes past retention are surfaced to their owner, who
          keeps or purges them. R11's "30 days cold, then purge" becomes
          "30 days, then ask."

[LATER]   AUTO-FILING: egzos files incoming content for the user. Wanted as
          an extension of the system; not built now.


================================================================================
AA. AMENDMENT — EVERY TOKEN IS BOUND TO ONE CONTAINER (amends §S's mapping
    "a user session (no client) → principal: interactive" and §T's "the
    browser presents the user's Supabase session to the container
    directly"; Egzos/egzos#282)
================================================================================

[DECIDED] Decided by the Chief's merge of Egzos/egzos#282 (drafted by the
          operator on a1r's and a6's review of it; the Chief may veto by
          reverting). Why: a provider session is valid at every
          container that trusts the provider, so a container that received
          a person's session could present it at another container the
          same person can reach.

[DECIDED] No container accepts a bare provider session. Each container is
          a public OAuth client of the provider; a person reaches it with a
          token the provider's OAuth 2.1 server issued to that container's
          client (PKCE), and an agent with a token issued to a client
          registered on that container. A token bound to one container is
          refused at every other.

[DECIDED] What does not change: one sign-in covers every container — no
          second password, no second login (§T). egzos.io obtains each
          container's token for the person through the provider; the
          consent page approves a person's own containers without asking
          again. Principal: the container's own client → interactive; a
          registered agent client → client. Contract: identity.md §3a.


================================================================================
AB. AMENDMENT — AGENTS: EACH PERSON REGISTERS THEIR OWN (amends §S's agent
    registry; replaces contract v1.1's rule that only an admin registers an
    agent, to serve that admin; Egzos/egzos#292)
================================================================================

[DECIDED] Decided by the Chief on 2026-10-23, answering the operator's
          questions; recorded by the operator, enacted by #292's merge;
          the Chief may veto by reverting. Why, in the operator's words: an
          agent acts for one person, on that person's grant, so that person
          is the one who consents to it; the admin-only rule left every
          other granted person without an agent of their own.

[DECIDED] ANYONE HOLDING A USER GRANT REGISTERS AGENTS THAT SERVE
          THEMSELVES, from an interactive principal, with the confirm (§U),
          never beyond their own grant: a registration's capabilities and
          scopes lie within the registrant's grant, and at check time the
          agent still holds only what both cover. So registration needs no
          publish: the agent holds no more than its person. An admin
          registers for themselves the same way. Nobody registers an agent
          to serve someone else. Contract: identity.md §4, rest.md §4.3.

[DECIDED] REVOCATION is by the person a registration serves, or an admin.
          User grants are outside this decision and stay an admin's act
          (contract v1.1). Contract: identity.md §4, rest.md §4.3.


================================================================================
AC. AMENDMENT — UPLOADS NEVER WRITTEN AS ITEMS ARE KEPT AND SHOWN (applies
    §Z to uploads; Egzos/egzos#292)
================================================================================

[DECIDED] Decided by the Chief on 2026-10-23, answering the operator's
          questions; recorded by the operator, enacted by #292's merge;
          the Chief may veto by reverting. Why: §Z, nothing is deleted
          automatically, holds for bytes that arrived but never became an
          item, as it does for staged bytes past retention.

[DECIDED] AN UPLOAD NEVER WRITTEN AS AN ITEM IS KEPT AND SHOWN to whoever
          uploaded it, to keep or delete: listed to its opener, an agent's
          to the person the agent serves (§AB), and to an admin, and
          removed only by an explicit discard, never on a timer.
          Contract: rest.md §4.4.

[DECIDED] A PER-PERSON CAP ON STAGED BYTES. Under §AB a person's agents
          count toward that person's cap, never a cap of their own.
          Contract: rest.md §4.4.


================================================================================
AD. AMENDMENT — CONFIRM CREDENTIALS FOLLOW GITHUB'S SUDO MODEL (amends §U:
    how the credential behind the biometric confirm is added and removed;
    Egzos/egzos#292)
================================================================================

[DECIDED] Decided by the Chief on 2026-10-23, answering the operator's
          questions with "how does GitHub handle this dilemma? follow
          that"; the rules below are the operator's reading of GitHub's
          model; recorded by the operator, enacted by #292's merge; the
          Chief may veto by reverting. Why: GitHub gates a change to an
          account's sign-in factors behind a recent re-authentication
          (sudo mode), lists and records every change, and recovers a lost
          factor through a stronger path (recovery codes). egzos is
          stricter in one place: the provider sign-in may be only an email
          link, so once a person has an authenticator, it is the stronger
          factor.

[DECIDED] THE FIRST CREDENTIAL is enrolled under a fresh sign-in, as
          GitHub's sudo mode asks (the provider token's most recent
          authentication, its amr, within the contract's 300 seconds), with
          the button as the act. Contract: identity.md §5, rest.md §4.3.

[DECIDED] EVERY FURTHER ADD, AND EVERY REMOVAL BY THE PERSON THEMSELVES,
          NEEDS A BIOMETRIC from one of that person's own existing
          credentials, never the button. Contract: identity.md §5,
          rest.md §4.3.

[DECIDED] RECOVERY: an admin removes another person's credentials with the
          admin's own biometric, never the button; the owner Token (the CLI
          or the lifeboat, egzos's analogue of GitHub's recovery codes)
          removes any. The person then enrols again as a first credential.
          Contract: rest.md §4.3.

[DECIDED] EVERY ADD AND REMOVE IS AUDITED, and a person's credentials are
          listed with created_at and last_used. Contract: rest.md §4.3.

[DECIDED] NO BUTTON ONCE A PERSON HAS A CREDENTIAL, on any origin: every
          confirm of theirs then needs it. Kept by the Chief on 2026-10-23
          in choosing how #285's two drafts were combined ("no plain button
          once someone has Face ID set up"). A credential belongs to the
          origin it was made on, as a security key registered with GitHub
          works only there, so a person with a credential on one origin is
          refused the button on another; they enrol there through
          recovery, or confirm on the origin that holds their credential.
          Contract: identity.md §5, rest.md §4.2.


================================================================================
AE. AMENDMENT — WHERE THE APP LIVES, HOW PEOPLE SIGN IN, AND THE CALLBACK
    WHILE egzos.io IS UNBOUGHT (amends identity.md §3a's egzos.io callback
    for an interim; Egzos/egzos#298)
================================================================================

[DECIDED] Decided by the Chief on 2026-10-23, answering the operator's
          questions; recorded by the operator, enacted by #298's merge; the
          Chief may veto by reverting.

[DECIDED] THE APP LIVES ON THE HOMEPAGE'S ORIGIN, at /app; the live demo
          stays at /. One origin carries the sign-in callback (identity.md
          §3a), the origins the door answers CORS for (identity.md §6) and the Face ID
          credentials (§AD). Egzos/egzos-platform's 2D apps/ui-flagship is
          parked.

[DECIDED] SIGN-IN: an email one-time code and GitHub, both through
          Supabase Auth (§T). Google, Apple and passkeys come later.

[DECIDED] UNTIL egzos.io IS BOUGHT, https://egzos-site.vercel.app stands in
          for https://egzos.io: a container's client registers
          https://egzos-site.vercel.app/oauth/callback in place of
          https://egzos.io/oauth/callback (identity.md §3a), and its
          identity.browser_origins names that origin. The Chief buys
          egzos.io before the Face ID screens ship, so no person's
          credential is made on the stand-in origin: the app offers no
          credential enrolment there. On the switch, each container's
          client is registered again with the egzos.io callback, the
          stand-in callback and origin leave every client's redirect URIs
          and every container's identity.browser_origins, and
          identity.client_id is set to match.


================================================================================
AF. AMENDMENT — WHERE A HOSTED CONTAINER'S STATE LIVES AND RUNS, AND ITS
    OWNER TOKEN (reads storage.md's [0.3 · 5] for a managed Postgres; answers
    identity.md §4's TODO(chief) on hosted provisioning; Egzos/egzos#319)
================================================================================

[DECIDED] Decided by the Chief on 2026-10-25, answering the operator's
          questions; recorded by the operator, enacted by #319's merge; the
          Chief may veto by reverting. The operator's own calls made with
          these are the contracts' a1p clauses, not decisions recorded
          here, among them one writer per container (storage.md §3.6),
          where a hosted container's keys and secrets live (identity.md
          §4, storage.md §3.7) and downloads through the container
          (storage.md §4).

[DECIDED] A MANAGED POSTGRES THAT ONLY THE CONTAINER'S OPERATOR ADMINISTERS
          IS THE OPERATOR'S OWN SUBSTRATE under storage.md's [0.3 · 5], so
          ContainerState may live on Supabase's Postgres. The database
          vendor joins the ledger's trust path, as §T recorded for the
          identity provider. The chain is hashed, not signed: audit verify
          catches an edit only while every later entry is left as it was.
          An entry re-hashed with every entry after it verifies, as does a
          chain whose last entries are gone, a restore included. The
          question first put to the Chief claimed more; the operator
          corrected it, and the Chief confirmed the decision with this
          reach the same day, asking that the outside anchor that would
          catch those, each place recording the cloud's head when it
          pulls, come with sync (§V). Contract: storage.md §1.

[DECIDED] ONE SUPABASE PROJECT PER HOSTED CONTAINER, holding its database
          and its Storage. Auth stays in the identity project (§T).
          Contract: storage.md §3.7, §4.

[DECIDED] THE POSTGRES DRIVER IS psycopg 3, as an optional extra, chosen
          knowing its licence, LGPL-3.0, which the question named.

[DECIDED] POSTGRES RUNS IN THE REQUIRED tests CHECK: a postgres service
          container joins the tests job, and a test fails when the
          postgres case goes missing. No new check name. The workflow is
          the Chief's commit.

[DECIDED] ITEMS WRITTEN IN THE SAME SECOND LIST BY ID, NEWEST FIRST, on
          every backend (created_at DESC, id DESC), so sqlite and postgres
          list alike. Text search stays as it runs.
          Contract: storage.md §2.

[DECIDED] ONE FLY APP PER HOSTED CONTAINER (§S's managed host): one
          machine, the small volume that is its home, and its own secrets,
          so no machine holds another container's credentials. Its calls
          to its database stay synchronous, which one person's container
          bears.

[DECIDED] THE HOST IS FLY.IO, and a container egzos hosts may serve plain
          HTTP to Fly's own TLS-terminating proxy on Fly's private network
          (amending [0.3 · 9] for hosted containers). Decided by the Chief
          on 2026-10-30, after a comparison with Railway, Render, Cloud Run
          and plain servers. Fly's default private network is shared by
          every app in an organization, so each hosted container's app
          gets a custom private network of its own, which only Fly's
          proxy reaches (a6, GHSA-558w-mv69-53cm). Contract: rest.md §1.

[DECIDED] THE OWNER TOKEN OF A CONTAINER egzos PROVISIONS is minted at
          provisioning and shown once, like recovery codes (§AD). The
          server keeps only its hash, and there is no keychain.json on the
          host. It is shown on the container's own page: from its own
          origin, to the owner signed in through the provider, never
          cached and never in a URL, so egzos's servers never see it.
          Contract: identity.md §4.


================================================================================
AG. AMENDMENT — HOW A TERMINAL SIGNS IN TO A CLOUD, AND WHAT SIGNS PEOPLE IN
    (gives §S's "the CLI … signs in to a cloud through Supabase" its shape;
    amends §AE's sign-in list; identity.md §3a, §8; Egzos/egzos#361)
================================================================================

[DECIDED] Decided by the Chief on 2026-11-05, on the operator's research
          into how Claude Code and GitHub's CLIs hand a browser sign-in
          back to a terminal, how their MCP services authenticate, and
          what the provider's OAuth 2.1 server offers (authorization code
          with PKCE and refresh tokens; no device grant; redirect URIs
          matched exactly); recorded by the operator, enacted by #361's
          merge; the Chief may veto by reverting.

[DECIDED] `egzos login` SIGNS A TERMINAL IN THROUGH egzos.io (option A of
          three). The CLI makes the PKCE pair and a state and opens the
          browser at egzos.io. egzos.io, signed in as the person (§T),
          runs the authorization-code flow for the person's cloud
          container's own client, from its own record (§AA; identity.md
          §3a), with the terminal's challenge in place of its own. Its
          callback page hands the code back to the terminal: to 127.0.0.1
          on the port the terminal named, when the terminal listens, or
          shown on the page to paste when it cannot (SSH, a headless
          machine). The terminal exchanges the code with the verifier it
          kept; the token is the person's, bound to that cloud, principal
          interactive, exactly identity.md §3a's sentence. The page never
          holds a usable credential, and the provider never sees a
          loopback redirect, so its exact match on redirect URIs does not
          bind the terminal's port. This is how Claude Code signs in; the
          paste path is its fallback for a terminal no browser can reach.

[DECIDED] REJECTED: B, the local registering itself as its own OAuth client
          with a loopback redirect (the token then names the local, which
          the cloud refuses under §AA; making the cloud accept it yields a
          client principal, which cannot confirm). C, a device flow, which
          is how GitHub's CLI signs in (the provider has none, §S retired
          ours, §R forbids building one). Device code stays retired.

[DECIDED] THE TERMINAL'S EXPERIENCE: one command; the browser opens; a
          paste path when it cannot come back; the refresh token in the
          operating system's credential store, a 0600 file when there is
          none; silent refresh; `egzos whoami` says who is signed in and
          where; `egzos logout` forgets the token on this machine (the
          provider publishes no revocation endpoint, so it can do no
          more). The CLI keeps the local owner Token for everything local
          (§S). The verbs: `egzos login` is for the person; `egzos
          connect` stays for agents (an MCP client's token: stdio today,
          the HTTP header one-liner for hosts without OAuth next).

[DECIDED] WHAT THE LOGIN IS FOR, IN ORDER: the local's link (the sign-in
          supplies the `sub` identity.md §4's owner grant needs, so no one
          types it), then §V's push and pull on the token it holds. The
          login needs a cloud: egzos.io runs the flow for the person's
          hosted container, and a person without one is told so in one
          line. The local's own client registration is not this login's
          (identity.md §3a's TODO on how a self-hosted container's link
          reaches egzos's record stays open; a local with no cloud links
          by hand, as today).

[DECIDED] AGENTS FROM ANY PLATFORM: the door built (#293, #310) is the
          design and no new one is drawn: /mcp over Streamable HTTP with
          RFC 9728 metadata, the provider's dynamic client registration,
          consent at egzos.io, and a client Token in the Authorization
          header for hosts without OAuth (identity.md §7). What remains:
          the agent consent page (egzos-platform#117), a connect page with
          each host's one-liner, and two checks before anyone relies on
          it: that Claude Code's registration path reaches /mcp on this
          provider (its loopback port must be pinned, since the provider
          matches redirect URIs exactly and has no port exemption), and
          that a public client is issued a refresh token.

[DECIDED] SIGN-IN: GOOGLE JOINS §AE's LIST NOW: an email one-time code,
          GitHub and Google, all through Supabase Auth; Apple and passkeys
          stay later. Identities with the same verified email are linked
          to one user automatically (the provider's default), so one
          person keeps one `sub` and one grant; manual linking stays off.
          The Chief registers the GitHub OAuth App and the Google OAuth
          client and enters both at the provider; nothing in either
          repository holds their secrets.

[LEAN]    A custom domain for the provider (auth.egzos.io) once egzos.io is
          bought, so Google's consent screen names egzos, not the project.


================================================================================
AH. AMENDMENT — THE TERMINAL ASKS BEFORE IT KEEPS A SIGN-IN (amends §AG's
    terminal sign-in; identity.md §3a, §8; Egzos/egzos#366)
================================================================================

[DECIDED] Decided by the Chief on 2026-11-07, answering the operator's
          question on a review finding against #364, tracked privately;
          recorded by the operator, enacted by #366's merge; the Chief may
          veto by reverting.

[DECIDED] BEFORE IT KEEPS ANYTHING, `egzos login` SHOWS WHO AND WHERE AND
          ASKS: the account the token names, its email first, and the
          cloud's origin. It keeps them only on the person's explicit yes,
          typed at that terminal. A login with no terminal to ask at is
          refused, and no flag or variable stands in for the yes.

[DECIDED] THE MATCHING CODE IS SHOWN ON BOTH SCREENS: the terminal prints
          it before the browser opens, and egzos.io's start page shows the
          same code, so the person can see that the page belongs to the
          terminal they are at (a6's question on egzos-platform#152).

[DECIDED] UNTIL THE CONFIRMATION LANDS, in R1's PR after #364, the
          terminal keeps without asking, and no code presents the stored
          token. (It landed in #367 on 2026-11-07; the account
          line shows the `sub` when the email fails the provider-id rule.)

AI. AMENDMENT — THE COMMAND LINE MOVES TO ITS OWN REPOSITORY, AND THE CORE
    TAKES THE NAME egzoscore (amends §Y's repositories and what §AG and §AH
    call "the terminal"; identity.md §8; rest.md §4)
================================================================================

[DECIDED] Decided by the Chief on 2026-11-13 and 2026-11-14; recorded by the
          operator; the Chief may veto by reverting.

[DECIDED] THE COMMAND PEOPLE TYPE IS ITS OWN PROGRAM IN ITS OWN REPOSITORY,
          Egzos/cli: MIT-licensed, written in TypeScript, shipped as one
          file per platform (npm `egzos`, an installer; Homebrew later). It
          keeps the name `egzos`. It reaches a container only through the
          door (rest.md) and holds no part of the core.

[DECIDED] THE DOOR CLIENT IS PUBLISHED WITH IT, under MIT, as
          `@egzos/client`: the code that presents a person's token to a
          container's door. It carries nothing of the flagship.

[DECIDED] THE PYTHON PACKAGE BECOMES `egzoscore`: the container (`init`,
          `serve`, `web`, `token`, `audit`, `config`, `link`) and the
          store, trust and ledger behind it. The rename waits until the new
          command covers the everyday commands; until then both exist, and
          `egzos` 0.1.x on PyPI is left as it is.

[DECIDED] WHAT MOVES TO THE NEW COMMAND: `login`, `logout`, `whoami` for a
          cloud, the everyday verbs on a cloud (ls, find, fetch, cat, get,
          add, mk, mv, cp, rm), and later people, agents, keys and
          `connect` on a cloud. §AG and §AH bind the new program exactly
          as they bound the old one: the hand-off, its checks, the
          question before a sign-in is kept, and no flag or variable that
          stands in for the yes.

[DECIDED] `login` LEAVES THE CORE AT ONCE (the Chief, 2026-11-14). The
          core's `egzos login` is removed, with its tests; nothing in the
          core signs a terminal in to a cloud. One program does: the new
          command, which keeps a sign-in under names of its own. A sign-in
          the core's command kept on a machine is removed there by hand;
          the new command never reads it.

[DECIDED] A COMMAND NAMES ITS PLACE. `cloud:` in front of a path is the
          person's cloud; no prefix is this machine. The first line of
          every answer says which place it came from, and as whom; a
          command that prints an item's own text (`cat`) prints that text
          alone, so it can be piped. A command that names the cloud and
          cannot reach it stops: it never falls back to this machine.

[DECIDED] THE TERMINAL STILL NEVER GIVES A CONFIRM (identity.md §8). A
          human-only act begun in a terminal is finished in the browser.

[LATER]   The new command driving a container on this machine through
          `egzoscore`; a place that sticks to a directory (`cd`); push and
          pull (§V); signing in on Windows, where the new command says it
          cannot yet.

[OPEN→CHIEF] The new command's first version number. Whether its macOS
          builds are signed with a Developer ID (unsigned, the Keychain
          asks again after every upgrade).

AJ. AMENDMENT — EACH SIGNED-IN TERMINAL IS A CLIENT OF ITS OWN (amends §AA's
    principal mapping, with a third: a registered terminal's client →
    interactive; §AG's terminal sign-in and its `egzos logout` sentence; and
    the second accepted residual identity.md §8 records under §AG.
    identity.md §3, §3a, §4, §5, §8; rest.md §4.2, §4.3, §6; Egzos/egzos#388)
================================================================================

[DECIDED] Decided by the Chief on 2026-11-14, choosing the third of three
          ways the operator set out for the app to show a terminal that is
          signed in (Egzos/egzos-platform#379): a note the browser keeps; a
          record the container keeps on the terminal's own word; or each
          terminal a client of its own. Recorded by the operator, enacted
          by #388's merge; the Chief may veto by reverting.

[DECIDED] EACH SIGNED-IN TERMINAL IS A CLIENT OF ITS OWN AT THE PROVIDER,
          AND THE PERSON'S CONTAINER HOLDS IT AS THAT PERSON'S OWN DEVICE:
          a third kind of record beside a person's grant and an agent's
          registration. It keeps the person's powers. What changes is
          that the container can tell it from the browser and from every
          other terminal: every request is attributable to that terminal
          on the chain, the app lists terminals with when each was last
          used, and revoking one works: its next request is refused.

          THE OPERATOR'S BINDING, which the Chief did not decide and may
          veto clause by clause (each is marked a1p in the contracts):

          - egzos.io registers the terminal's client, when the person
            continues on the start page. The option as put to the Chief
            said `egzos login` registers it. Bound this way the provider
            still sees no loopback redirect and the hand-off of §AG and
            §AH keeps its shape, which is also why this is not the B that
            §AG rejected (the local registering itself with a loopback
            redirect, for a token the cloud refuses under §AA or accepts
            only as a client principal).
          - The person confirms the terminal at their container before
            the provider issues, as they confirm an agent (§AB, §U). For
            a person with no confirm credential that takes a sign-in at
            most five minutes old, so `egzos login` may ask them to sign
            in again.
          - The person stays the actor of what is done at a terminal;
            each entry names the terminal beside them.
          - A terminal has a name, shown before it is kept.
          - The person, an admin, or the terminal itself ends it. The
            last is `egzos logout`, which now ends the terminal at the
            cloud before it forgets the token: that amends §AG's "it can
            do no more".
          - A terminal's token concludes no confirm and gives no one
            access, which holds §AI's "the terminal still never gives a
            confirm" at the container.
          - At a person's first registered terminal, egzos.io ends the
            sign-ins terminals kept before this, which name the
            container's own client.
          - It is what the app draws as the house beside the orb, which
            the Chief asked for on 2026-11-13.

          UNTIL THE CODE LANDS (this repository's door, egzos.io's
          hand-off pages, the command in Egzos/cli), a terminal signs in
          as §AG has it, with a token issued to the container's own
          client.

[LATER]   A terminal that holds less than its person (one project, or
          reading only). Removing the provider's record of a client that
          no registration names any more.

[OPEN→CHIEF] The name a terminal shows by default: the machine's name,
          which then leaves the machine and is kept at the cloud, or a
          name typed at `egzos login`. The operator's draft takes the
          machine's name, printed before the browser opens and shown
          before it is kept, with `--name` to give another.

[DECIDED] The Chief, on 2026-11-15, passing the journeys for the above
          (Egzos/egzos-platform#388), asked that the app show what type
          of machine the command line is connecting from, so that it is
          in what the cloud records of a terminal too. The operator took
          the ask as the decision to show it and records it here,
          enacted by the merge that closes Egzos/egzos#394; the Chief
          may veto by reverting.

          A TERMINAL MAY SAY WHAT KIND OF MACHINE IT IS, IN ONE LINE
          BESIDE ITS NAME (identity.md §3a, §8; rest.md §4.3;
          storage.md §3.2). THE OPERATOR'S BINDING, each clause marked
          a1p in the contracts:

          - The line is the name's twin: optional, the terminal's own
            claim, held to the name's rule, shown before it is kept and
            labelled wherever it is shown. Nothing checks it and
            nothing is decided on it.
          - The confirm that registers the terminal is bound to it,
            with the name.
          - The container keeps it on the terminal's registration. On
            the chain it writes it where it writes the name: in the
            read that shows the confirm, each time one is shown, and
            not in the entry that records the registration. Entries
            made at the terminal afterwards name the terminal, not the
            line. That is the operator's reading of the Chief's word
            "telemetry", and his to widen.
          - A container from before this refuses a request that carries
            the line; egzos.io then registers the terminal without it.

[OPEN→CHIEF] What the line holds by default. The operator's draft: the
          kind of computer and its operating system, and nothing that
          tells one machine from another of its kind (no serial number,
          no hardware identifier, no network address), printed with the
          name before the browser opens, with `--machine` to give
          another and `--no-machine` to give none.


================================================================================
AK. AMENDMENT — A PERSON RENAMES AN ITEM OR A PLACE; THE DOOR SAYS WHAT IT
    SERVES (amends container.md §2's rename sentence, which bound only a
    rename that happens on its own; [0.3 · 2]'s capture naming, which now
    writes a `/` or a `:` as `-` and drops Cc, Zl, Zp and Bidi_Control
    characters;
    rest.md §4.2 item 1's list of confirm-gated acts, which gains the
    rename of a verified or promoted item and of a place, item 3's
    binding, which gains an item's version, scope and trust status
    and a place's name, and item 4's fresh answer, which carries the
    act's first-leg fields as they now stand; storage.md §3.3's
    challenge binding, likewise.
    rest.md §4, §4.1, §4.2, §4.5, §4.6, §5, §8; container.md §2;
    context-item.md §3, §6; identity.md §4, §5; storage.md §3, §3.3;
    events.md §1; Egzos/egzos#404, Egzos/egzos#360)
================================================================================

[DECIDED] Decided by the Chief on 2026-11-25 and 2026-11-26. On
          2026-11-25 he asked for one press-and-hold wheel in the app
          that carries every act on a thing, and for the app to add a
          thread or a project and to add, move, or copy files. On
          2026-11-26 he answered six questions about the wheel; asked
          whether rename and remove are in its first build, he said:
          "Do everything, start it all". No route renamed an item or a
          place (#404). This section binds renaming; removing a place
          follows in its own change. Recorded by the operator, enacted
          by the merge of the contract change; the Chief may veto by
          reverting.

[DECIDED] A PERSON RENAMES AN ITEM AND A PLACE FROM THE APP.

          THE OPERATOR'S BINDING, which the Chief did not decide and may
          veto clause by clause (each is marked a1p in the contracts,
          and not running until its code lands):

          - Renaming an item is a person's act, as a tombstone is: an
            interactive principal holding `organize` and `fetch` where
            the item sits; an agent is refused as for anything absent.
            It sets an artifact's file name, or a text item's title,
            marked as a person's (`title_engine: person`) so no title
            pass replaces it, and nothing else. Event `item.rename`,
            with the old name and the new.
          - Renaming an item that is verified, or that a person has
            promoted, takes the confirm, as its tombstone does: the
            confirm shows the old name and the new, and is bound to the
            new. Any other item is renamed at once, an unverified rule
            aside, which is refused whatever its provenance.
          - A confirm on an item (promote, a gated tombstone or rename,
            a move or copy's confirm, and an approve, for each item its
            proposal names) is bound to the item's version, scope and
            trust status as its first leg read them, so a second leg
            that finds any of the three changed concludes `mismatch` and
            changes nothing; the person asks again, and the fresh answer
            shows the act as it now stands. Every act that changes an
            item moves one of the three: a rename the version, in the
            same step as its write (a door serves the rename only so,
            and only where every confirm on an item is bound to the
            three); a promote the status and the version; a move the
            scope; a quarantine the status; a tombstone ends the item; a
            title pass, where one runs, the version with the title it
            writes. A title pass aside, only an act its own rule admits
            and the chain records moves what a confirm is bound to. So a
            principal whose rule admits such an act, an agent holding
            `organize` among them, can keep a person's confirm from
            concluding; each act is on the chain and revoking that
            principal ends it. A `mismatch` says nothing of why.
          - Renaming a place is the container's admin's act, behind the
            confirm, and the place is a project or a thread; a place of
            any other type gets the one refusal (a1p). It needs a person
            holding a provider token whose grant holds `admin` over the
            whole container, as reading the grants needs (a container
            token gets the one refusal, as there), with `organize` and
            `fetch` on the place; any such person may, the owner or
            another admin. After a rename a path names whatever bears
            the name now. The rename changes no coverage and no
            audience, since tokens, grants and registrations hold ids;
            it changes only what a path names. So it is kept to the
            container's admin, who already decides who may see and act
            on every place, and made a confirmed act the chain records
            (`node.rename`, with the old name and the new). The name it
            frees is free: anyone whose token covers a parent, a person
            or an agent, may make a place that bears it, before the
            rename or after, and whatever is still addressed by the old
            path, a read, a write, a grant or a registration, then
            reaches that place, without the confirm; a move or a copy
            still passes the gate. The door keeps no old name to refuse
            this by; that is why a client keeps ids. The node keeps no
            old name and no route serves one, so nothing is capped (the
            chain keeps the old name in `node.rename`, for the owner's
            audit, and a proposal parked before the rename keeps the
            path it was parked with, which the door never serves); a
            path beneath it shows its new name to whoever reads that
            path, a person or an agent, its ancestors' names included,
            as every path already does, and so shows that it was renamed
            and when (decided below). The confirm shows the old name and
            the new,
            and is bound to the node's name as its first leg read it and
            to the new; a name renamed away and back between the legs
            matches again. Renaming an item or a place to the name it
            bears now changes nothing and opens no confirm. Its id
            stays; the node alone is written, in one atomic step with
            the confirm's `step_up` and its `node.rename`. Grants and
            agent registrations keep node ids, as the door already does.
            The inbox, the personal root and `global` are never renamed,
            and no other type but a project or a thread is renamed in
            this change.
            A proposal is shown with its places' names as they stand,
            never as they stood when it was parked, and a door serves a
            place's rename only so. A client keeps a place's id, never
            its path.
          - A place's name, made or renamed on any surface, is 1 to 255
            Unicode scalar values, compared as given with no
            normalisation, with no `/`, no `:`, and no character of
            category Cc, Zl or Zp or with Bidi_Control, and never the
            one character `*`. An item's new name keeps an upload name's
            rule and holds none of those characters. A lone surrogate is
            refused. Existing names stay. Pure capture writes a `/` or a
            `:` in a title as `-` and drops every Cc, Zl, Zp or
            Bidi_Control character, then keeps the first 40 characters,
            then names a thread left with nothing, or only `*`, by the
            item's id.
          - The door serves what it carries (`GET /v1/limits`): the
            contract's version, a word for each thing it serves that
            0.2.0 did not (`terminals.machine`, `items.rename`,
            `scopes.rename`), and the upload limits #360 asked for. It
            reads two config keys and one constant, and is not a config
            surface. A container from before it answers the one
            refusal, which a client reads as "none of these", so it
            never takes a missing route for a refusal of the act.

[DECIDED] A PLACE'S RENAME SHOWS ITS NEW NAME, THAT IT WAS RENAMED, AND
          WHEN,
          to whoever can read a path beneath it, a person or an agent,
          without seeing the place itself. On 2026-11-26 the Chief was
          asked: "A renamed project or thread shows its new name to anyone
          who can see something inside it." (the operator's pick: yes). He
          said: "Rename, yeah, it's fine if it shows." Asked the same
          evening: "the new name shows right away, to people and agents who
          can see inside, for any place.", he said: "For number 5, yes. Go
          ahead with that." A path names every place above a thing, seen or
          not, so such a reader's paths show the new name from the moment
          the rename lands, and a path through the old name no longer
          reaches the place. Recorded by the operator.

[LATER]   Unique names among siblings, and which type of place may sit
          under which; left out because pure capture names inbox
          threads from titles that may repeat.

[LATER]   Removing a place, in its own change.

[LATER]   Renaming a place of a type other than a project or a thread;
          this change renames those two.

[LATER]   A person who is not the container's admin renaming a place
          they made; it needs a rule for names a rename re-points.

[OPEN→CHIEF] What removing a place that still holds things should do:
          refuse it, or one act that sends what it holds to the inbox
          first, under the gate. It belongs to the later change that
          removes a place.

[OPEN→CHIEF] Whether two places side by side may share a name. The draft
          lets them, as today; a path that names both is refused as
          ambiguous, and the person gives a longer path or the id.


================================================================================
AL. AMENDMENT — AN APPROVED AGENT SAVES AND READS EVERY KIND OF FILE
    THROUGH THE MCP DOOR, AND ITS FILE IS KEPT AT ONCE (amends rest.md
    §4.4 item 3's staging of an agent's artifact and storage.md §4's
    staging rule for agent-proposed artifacts, for artifacts written
    from now on; adds a single-use address for an upload's bytes beside
    rest.md §6's grant. rest.md §4, §4.4, §4.6, §4.7, §5, §6, §8;
    storage.md §3.5, §4; identity.md §7; context-item.md §3;
    Egzos/egzos#405. The letter was held for this change by an earlier
    draft that never merged)
================================================================================

[DECIDED] Decided by the Chief on 2026-11-26, in three answers, recorded
          by the operator with each as he gave it; enacted by the merge
          that records this section; the Chief may veto by reverting.

          (1) Asked what files an outside agent must be able to save into
          his cloud's chosen projects and threads, 2026-11-26: "Golden
          files can be ... everything. The MCP and the CLI and every other
          [door] has to be able to ... do all of the ... files and formats
          and everything under the ... sun all at ... once." (The
          ellipses are pauses in his speech, kept; "[door]" is ours.) So
          every door carries any file of any format.

          (2) Asked, the same evening, whether an approved agent's file
          is kept at once in the places its person ticked on the approve
          screen, or held in the person's 16 slots until the person
          decides: "go with keep." The page he answered also proposed a
          size limit per agent, and that the file stays marked as the
          agent's and unverified.

          (3) Asked, the same evening, how a file too large for one tool
          call travels: "In terms of what the research says section, go
          with the outcome of the research that was suggested." The
          research found the common way: a tool hands back a one-time
          upload address and the agent's own code sends the bytes there
          (Notion, Slack, Box, Egnyte, ClickUp, AWS and Cloudinary do
          this; the MCP standard itself defines no file upload).

          Already in the contract, and not reopened: an agent may be given
          the whole container (§AM).

[DECIDED] THE MCP DOOR CARRIES EVERY KIND OF FILE. A small file rides in
          one call; any larger one goes through an upload whose bytes go
          to a single-use address. A file is read back by name, type and
          size, and its bytes through rest.md §6's grant.

[DECIDED] AN APPROVED AGENT'S FILE IS KEPT AT ONCE, in a place its terms
          cover, the whole container where its person gave it that. It
          stays the agent's and unverified, and a person promotes it or
          removes it as any unverified item.

          THE OPERATOR'S BINDING, which the Chief did not decide and may
          veto clause by clause (each is marked a1p in the contracts, and
          not running until the code lands):

          - One rule for every tool: it mirrors a route the door already
            has, under the same capabilities, coverage, validation,
            refusal and audit events, so no tool gives a caller a power
            its token lacks at `/v1/`. Where a tool needs something new,
            the route gets it first: the address has its own route,
            `POST /v1/uploads/{id}/address`, and every door may use it.
          - One call carries up to 131,072 bytes (128 KiB), checked by the
            length of its base64 before it is decoded, the same over stdio
            and HTTP: at `/mcp` that leaves room for the call inside the
            262,144 bytes the door reads of a request. The write is one
            atomic step, so a failed call leaves nothing behind.
          - The address is bound to the upload, its opener, the declared
            size and hash, and one use; it lives 900 seconds and never
            past the upload; it is redeemed with no bearer, on one path
            and one method, and is never a bearer for anything else. The
            bytes are checked against the declared length and hash on
            arrival.
          - An agent's kept bytes are bounded per agent: 1 GiB by default
            (`blobs.agent_kept_max_bytes`, which an admin may change), ten
            files at the per-file limit, so a busy agent fits and a
            runaway one stops long before a hosted container's volume
            fills. A person's own uploads count toward no agent's bound.
            At the bound an open answers `too_many_bytes`; a person frees
            room by removing the agent's files. Written files no longer
            hold any of the person's 16 slots; open and orphaned uploads
            still do. A place the agent's terms do not cover is refused,
            never held. `GET /v1/limits` names the bound, the one-call
            limit and, once all of this runs, the word `files.agent`.
          - A file's name keeps a place name's characters (§AK), on every
            door, and is display data only, never a path on any store.
          - `egzos_fetch` names files and mints no grant; `egzos_get`
            reads one item and carries its grant's address, on the
            container's public origin.
          - No tool makes a place: an agent saves into places its person
            made, and finds their names with `egzos_places`. A tool for it
            waits on a rule of its own at `POST /v1/scopes` for an agent: a
            capability, a bound on how many it makes, its places shown as
            its own, and a way for the person to remove one.
          - No tool for a human-only act, and none that fetches an address
            a caller chose.

          WHAT THE OTHER DOORS OWE, so that every door stays true: the
          REST door carries any file already and gains the address route
          and the keep; the command line carries any file already, with
          the owner's token, and changes nothing; egzos.io's app and the
          lifeboat show an agent's kept file as the agent's and unverified,
          and offer the person promote and remove on it, as on any
          unverified item.


================================================================================
AM. AMENDMENT — AN AGENT GETS WHAT ITS PERSON TICKS ON THE CONSENT SCREEN
    (gives §AB's "never beyond their own grant" the source of a
    registration's terms, which no contract named once identity.md §9
    retired authorization-server.md §7's binding to OAuth's scope
    parameter; replaces rest.md §4.3's check that an authorization
    "asks for no scopes beyond the body's"; the retired server's page
    took a request exactly as asked (spec/design/consent.md D-C2), and
    the page egzos.io hosts does not; rewrites identity.md §3a's check
    on Egzos/egzos#283, which was owed before the door shipped, as
    owed before agent sign-in, a terminal's registration and the
    first container egzos does not host, and restates what identity.md
    §3a and §8 say a client's token reaches at the provider; adds a
    word to §AK's list in rest.md §4.6. rest.md §4.3, §4.6; identity.md
    §3a, §4, §5, §8; Egzos/egzos#377, and the second question in the
    body of Egzos/egzos#308, on re-registration)
================================================================================

[DECIDED] Decided by the Chief on 2026-11-26, choosing the second of the
          two ways Egzos/egzos#377 sets out for where an agent
          registration's capabilities and scopes come from (a default
          the contract names, or the person's own choice on the consent
          page), after the operator's survey of how other MCP servers
          decide it: "go with the suggestion in the document, the
          closest to you. The screen lists your things and you tick
          what this agent gets." Recorded by the operator, enacted by
          the merge of the contract change; the Chief may veto by
          reverting.

[DECIDED] THE PERSON CHOOSES ON THE CONSENT SCREEN WHAT AN AGENT GETS, in
          the Chief's words above: the screen lists the person's things,
          and they tick what this agent gets.

[DECIDED] A PERSON WHO IS NOT THE ADMIN MAY SEE THEIR OWN ACCESS. Decided
          by the Chief on 2026-11-26. The question as put to him: "May
          a person who isn't the cloud's admin see their own access
          (what they can do, and in which places)? The screen needs it
          to list 'your things'." The operator's pick: yes. His words:
          "For number 1, go with your suggestion."

[DECIDED] AN AGENT ALREADY APPROVED IS CHOSEN FOR AGAIN, REPLACING WHAT
          IT HAD, WITH THE SCREEN SHOWING WHAT IS REPLACED. Decided by
          the Chief on 2026-11-26. The question as put to him: "An
          agent you already approved asks again. Do you choose again
          and replace what it had, with the screen showing what is
          being replaced, or is it refused until you end it?" The
          operator's pick: choose again and replace. His words:
          "Number 2, go with your suggestion." This answers the second
          question in the body of Egzos/egzos#308: re-registration is
          not refused. That the door's first leg is what tells the
          screen what is replaced is the operator's binding below.

[DECIDED] AN AGENT MAY BE GIVEN THE WHOLE CONTAINER. Decided by the
          Chief on 2026-11-26. The question as put to him: "May an
          agent ever be given the whole cloud, now and later?" The
          operator's pick: not offered for now, and refused at the
          door. His words, against that pick: "Number 3, yeah, I want
          an agent to be able to be given a whole cloud." How it is
          offered is the operator's binding below.

[DECIDED] AGENT SIGN-IN IS NOT SWITCHED ON BEFORE A LIVE TEST. Decided
          by the Chief on 2026-11-26. The question as put to him: "May
          agent sign-in be switched on before one live test with a
          real agent token at the sign-in provider?" The operator's
          pick: no. His words: "Number 4, and 4, go with what you
          suggest."

          THE OPERATOR'S BINDING, which the Chief did not decide and may
          veto clause by clause (each is marked a1p in the contracts;
          the read, the first leg's terms and what a registration
          replaces are not running until their code lands, which is
          together: no door serves the read without the other two,
          nor before §AK's rule on a place's name runs):

          - The terms are places, and what the agent may do in them,
            or the whole container, within the person's own grant
            (§AB), and come from that choice and from nowhere else.
            The provider's own scopes (openid, email, profile, phone)
            carry none of it.
          - The read is `GET /v1/grant`. It answers the caller's own
            capabilities and the ids of the places their grant names,
            and nothing else (an id holds the time its place was
            made): no name of a place, and nothing of any other
            person, agent or token. That "in which places" takes the
            id as it is, with that time, is the operator's reading;
            the question put to the Chief did not say so. It is
            served to a person signed in through the provider. An
            agent, a container token and a registered terminal's
            token are refused as for anything absent. A page refused
            it offers no choice.
          - The door enforces the bound and the binding, as it already
            runs. Terms wider than the person's own grant are refused
            before the confirm, and again inside its atomic step
            against the grant as it then stands. A choice of nothing
            is refused as malformed. The confirm is bound to the
            capabilities and the places, so no other terms can land.
            The first leg is to say the terms it bound, and the page
            to word the confirm from that answer; the chain is to
            hold them, on the owner's record.
          - The consent page owes the rest, since the door cannot see
            a screen. It offers only what the person's own grant
            bounds. Nothing is ticked until the person ticks it.
            Nothing the agent supplies selects, suggests, orders or
            ticks anything: not the provider's scope string, not any
            other part of its request, not what it registered about
            itself, not its name, and not the name of a place.
          - A place's name is its maker's text, the first words of
            what was written where a capture opened it, or, once
            §AK's rename runs, its renamer's text, drawn inert
            beside the place's kind and path, in an order the page
            states and no client steers. The choose step is not
            offered until the door keeps §AK's rule on a place's name
            (rest.md §4.5), which runs only once its code lands; the
            read of the person's grant is served only where it runs,
            and GET /v1/limits then names the word grants.own. The
            rule bars a path's separators, control and line-break
            characters and bidirectional controls, and bounds the
            length; it leaves other formatting characters and names
            that look alike. A name given before it is drawn inert
            all the same.
          - What the page sends is what it shows: capabilities by
            name, never a role bundle; places by id, never a path;
            one set of capabilities over every chosen place, since a
            registration holds one set; each place with everything
            beneath it, now and later; and that an agent covering a
            place may make a thread or a project under it.
          - The whole container is one choice of its own, offered only
            to a person whose grant holds it, never ticked for them,
            and worded plainly as everything in this cloud, what is
            made later and the inbox included. The page sends "*" for
            that choice alone, never by adding up ticked places. The
            door takes "*" for an agent only from a person whose grant
            holds "*", binds the confirm to it and records it on the
            chain, as it already runs. That is all the door holds to
            today. It is to say the terms in its first leg, to take
            "*" only alone, and to take ids alone on this route; none
            of the three runs yet. Ticking places, top places
            included, gives those places and what is under them; as
            the container runs today its two top places hold every
            place, so ticking both covers what "*" covers, and the
            page says so, but sends them as two places.
          - A place renamed between the choice and the confirm is
            still the place chosen, since the terms are ids. One that
            is gone, or no longer the person's to give, registers
            nothing. Nothing moves or removes a place today; a rename
            is §AK's, and runs once its code lands.
          - The provider's scopes are neither read nor shown. The
            container reads no scope from a token, as it already
            runs. The screen says, in fixed words of its own: that
            approving lets this agent sign in to this cloud as the
            person, within what they tick; and that the agent can
            read their account's record at the sign-in provider:
            their profile, their email, a phone number where the
            account holds one, and how they sign in. An
            authorization that names any scope but the provider's
            four is refused.
          - Those words hold only while the identity project gives
            nothing more to a token carrying a client's id: by the
            provider's documentation such a token holds what the
            person's own sign-in holds, whatever scopes were asked.
            So the consent page approves an agent only while two
            dated records of the operator's stand: that check, and
            the live test above against the provider release the
            project runs. A change to the project's rules, or another
            release, fells its record until it is made again. Without
            both the page denies the authorization at the provider
            and calls no route (identity.md §3a). The door checks
            neither record and cannot, and agents approved before a
            record fell stay until they are ended. The provider's own
            routes that change an account or approve a consent refuse
            such a token by a reading of its source (v2.199.0,
            2026-11-26); the test is to confirm it.
          - Choosing again is a new registration through the same
            screen, from nothing, which replaces the earlier one
            whole, and whose first leg shows what it replaces, in the
            whole-container choice's own words where either side is
            the whole container. Declining ends nothing, and the
            screen says so. For an approval the provider gave
            without asking, the page calls no route; the person ends
            the agent, and egzos.io withdraws their consent to it at
            the provider. An agent ended any other way is still
            consented there until that person's next visit to their
            agents on egzos.io, which withdraws it; this container
            refuses it meanwhile. Nothing narrows a registration in
            place.

[LATER]   One agent holding different capabilities in different
          places. Narrowing a live registration in place, from the
          app. A terminal reading its person's grant.

[LATER]   This section does not touch the staging of an agent's file
          (rest.md §4.4). The Chief's ruling of the same day on it
          (Egzos/egzos#405) is its own change.

[NOTE]    2026-11-27, the operator: a fact corrected, and the
          operator's binding above amended to match it; the Chief
          decided nothing here and may veto it as the rest of the
          binding. The provider takes a fifth scope word,
          offline_access, beside the four named above. It carries
          none of the terms either, and it decides nothing a client
          receives: a client is handed a refresh token with or
          without it (read in the provider's public source at
          release v2.199.0). Many agents' clients send the word. So
          two lines above are superseded: where the binding says the
          provider's own scopes are "(openid, email, profile,
          phone)", read those and offline_access; and where it says
          an authorization "that names any scope but the provider's
          four is refused", read five. The consent page's fixed
          words gain one sentence: that an approved agent stays
          signed in to this cloud, with no end date of its own,
          until its person or an admin ends its access, which was
          already so. rest.md §4.3 carries all of it.
